questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding Star?

I. It is made up of gases.

II. They do not have their own heat and light.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stars are made up of gases:** Stars are primarily composed of **hydrogen and helium gases**. These gases undergo nuclear fusion in the star's core, which produces energy in the form of light and heat. *Hence, Statement I is correct.*
 
• **Stars emit their own heat and light:** Unlike planets, stars generate their own **heat and light** through the process of nuclear fusion. This phenomenon occurs when hydrogen atoms fuse to form helium, releasing a significant amount of energy. *Hence, Statement II is incorrect.*
 
• **Stars are luminous celestial bodies:** Due to the energy produced in their cores, stars are visible as bright objects in the night sky. Their luminosity varies depending on their size, temperature, and stage of life.
 
• **Stars are the fundamental building blocks of galaxies:** Galaxies are massive systems consisting of billions of stars, along with gas, dust, and dark matter. Stars play a crucial role in the evolution of galaxies.
 
• **Examples of stars:** The **Sun** is the closest star to Earth and a perfect example of a star that emits its own light and heat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nuclear Fusion in Stars:**

 
 
• Stars produce energy through the process of **nuclear fusion**, where hydrogen nuclei fuse to form helium. This reaction releases a tremendous amount of energy, which powers the star and emits light and heat.
 
• The energy produced in the core travels outward to the surface, from where it radiates into space.
 
• This process is what makes stars self-luminous and distinguishes them from other celestial objects like planets or moons.
 
 
 
• **Types of Stars:**
 
 
• Stars are classified based on their **size, temperature, and luminosity**. Common types include **red dwarfs, white dwarfs, neutron stars, and supergiants**.
 
• For example, the Sun is a **G-type main-sequence star**, also known as a yellow dwarf.
 
 
 
• **Life Cycle of Stars:**
 
 
• Stars undergo a life cycle that includes stages such as **nebula, main sequence, red giant, and supernova**, depending on their initial mass.
 
• Massive stars may end their life as **neutron stars** or **black holes**.
 
 
 
• **Stars vs. Planets:**
 
 
• Unlike stars, planets do not produce their own light or heat. Instead, they reflect the light of a nearby star, like the Sun.
 
• Planets are made up of solids, liquids, and gases, while stars are predominantly made of gases undergoing nuclear fusion.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Stars:**
 
 
• Stars are essential for the formation of **elements heavier than helium**, which are dispersed into the universe during supernova explosions.
 
• They provide energy and heat necessary for sustaining life on planets, such as Earth.

questions.question: A 60 W electric lamp is used for 5 hours daily. Calculate the energy consumed in 'units' (kilowatt-hours) in 30 days.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**9 units**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• Electric energy consumption is measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh), also referred to as "units."
 
• To calculate the energy consumed, the formula is **Energy (kWh) = Power (kW) × Time (hours)**.
 
• The power of the lamp is given as 60 W, which is equivalent to **0.06 kW** (since 1 kW = 1000 W).
 
• Daily usage is 5 hours, so the daily energy consumption is **0.06 × 5 = 0.3 kWh.**
 
• For 30 days, the total energy consumed is **0.3 × 30 = 9 kWh.**

questions.question: Which of Rutherford's experimental observations led him to conclude that the positive charge of an atom is concentrated in a very small region?

options.text: Electrons were found to orbit the nucleus in specific energy levels.
A very small fraction of a-particles rebounded almost backwards.
Most a-particles followed a straight path through the gold foil.
A small fraction of α-particles were deflected by small angles.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A very small fraction of α-particles rebounded almost backwards.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rutherford's gold foil experiment involved the bombardment of a thin gold foil with α-particles (helium nuclei) to study atomic structure.
 
• Most α-particles passed through the foil undeflected, indicating that atoms are mostly empty space.
 
• A small fraction of α-particles were deflected at small angles, suggesting the presence of a positively charged center.
 
• A very tiny fraction of α-particles rebounded almost directly backward, leading Rutherford to conclude that the positive charge of the atom is concentrated in a very small, dense region, which he termed the nucleus.
 
• This observation provided experimental evidence for the nuclear model of the atom, replacing the earlier plum pudding model proposed by J.J. Thomson.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gold Foil Experiment:** Conducted in 1909 by Hans Geiger and Ernest Marsden under the supervision of Ernest Rutherford, this experiment was pivotal in understanding atomic structure.
 
• **Nuclear Model of the Atom:** Proposed by Rutherford, it describes the atom as having a dense central nucleus containing protons, with electrons orbiting in the empty space surrounding it.
 
• **Plum Pudding Model:** An earlier atomic model proposed by J.J. Thomson, which suggested that electrons were embedded in a positively charged "pudding-like" substance. This model was disproved by Rutherford's experiment.
 
• **α-Particles:** Positively charged particles consisting of two protons and two neutrons, used as projectiles in the gold foil experiment.
 
• **Implications of Rutherford's Findings:** The discovery of the nucleus laid the foundation for the development of the modern quantum mechanical model of the atom and further studies on subatomic particles.

questions.question: Which of the following hormone is associated with puberty in human males?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Testosterone**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Testosterone** is the primary male sex hormone responsible for the development of secondary sexual characteristics in males during **puberty**.
 
• It is produced mainly by the **testes** in males, with a small amount being produced by the adrenal glands.
 
• Testosterone levels rise significantly during puberty, leading to changes such as the development of facial and body hair, deepening of the voice, and increased muscle mass.
 
• It also plays a vital role in sperm production and the maintenance of libido in males.
 
• Hormonal imbalances in testosterone levels can lead to various health issues, such as delayed puberty or fertility problems in males.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Adrenaline:**

 
 
• Adrenaline, also known as epinephrine, is a hormone released by the **adrenal glands** in response to stress or danger.
 
• It is part of the body's "fight or flight" response and helps in increasing heart rate, blood flow to muscles, and energy availability.
 
• Adrenaline is not linked to the changes that occur during puberty.
 
 
 
• **Oestrogen:**
 
 
• Oestrogen is the primary female sex hormone, produced mainly by the **ovaries**.
 
• It is responsible for the development of female secondary sexual characteristics, such as breast development and regulation of the menstrual cycle.
 
• Although males have small amounts of oestrogen, it does not play a significant role in male puberty.
 
 
 
• **Thyroxin:**
 
 
• Thyroxin is a hormone produced by the **thyroid gland** and is essential for regulating metabolism, growth, and development.
 
• It is not directly involved in the hormonal changes associated with puberty.
 
• An imbalance in thyroxin can lead to conditions such as hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism, which may indirectly affect growth and development.
 
 
 
• **Testosterone:**
 
 
• It is a steroid hormone classified under **androgens**.
 
• Testosterone plays a critical role in the differentiation of male reproductive tissues such as the testes and prostate.
 
• It also influences behaviors such as aggression and competitiveness, which become more pronounced during puberty.
 
• Testosterone levels are typically higher in males than in females, contributing to the distinct physical differences between the sexes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Testosterone in Puberty:**

 
 
• Testosterone is responsible for the **growth of the male reproductive organs**, including the penis and testes.
 
• It stimulates the production of **sperm** in the testes, a process called spermatogenesis.
 
• The hormone also contributes to the development of secondary sexual characteristics, such as a deeper voice and facial hair.
 
 
 
• **Age of Onset of Puberty:**
 
 
• In boys, puberty typically begins between the ages of **9 and 14 years**.
 
• The increase in testosterone levels during this period triggers various physical and emotional changes.
 
 
 
• **Testosterone and Health:**
 
 
• Low testosterone levels in males can lead to **delayed puberty**, reduced muscle mass, and fatigue.
 
• High testosterone levels may result in **aggressive behavior** or other health issues.

questions.question: Which statement accurately describes outwash deposits?

options.text: Angular, unsorted debris left by stagnant ice
Sorted, rounded sediments from meltwater streams
Fine clay blown by wind in dry glacial areas
Large erratics dropped on steep glacier slopes

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sorted, rounded sediments from meltwater streams**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Outwash deposits**, also known as **glacio-fluvial deposits**, are materials that are picked up, transported, and eventually deposited by **meltwater streams** flowing from the front of a melting glacier.
 
• Because these sediments are transported by running water, they undergo a process of **sorting**. Heavier particles like **gravel** and **sand** settle first, while finer silts are carried further away.
 
• The action of water causes the debris to tumble and wear down, resulting in **rounded** edges, unlike the **angular** fragments found in direct glacial deposits.
 
• In contrast, **glacial till** (Option 1) is deposited directly by the ice and is characterized by being **unsorted** and **angular** because it has not been reworked by water.
 
• **Loess** (Option 3) refers to fine-grained, wind-blown deposits often found in periglacial environments, while **erratics** (Option 4) are large boulders transported far from their source by ice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A broad, gently sloping sheet of outwash deposits is known as an **outwash plain** or a **sandur**.
 
• **Eskers** are long, winding ridges of stratified sand and gravel, thought to be deposited by meltwater streams flowing through **ice tunnels** within or beneath a glacier.
 
• **Kames** are small, steep-sided mounds or hills composed of stratified drift that accumulated in depressions on the glacier surface before being deposited on the ground as the ice melted.
 
• The study of these deposits helps geologists reconstruct the **paleoclimate** and the movement patterns of ancient **ice sheets**.

questions.question: Which property of sound determines its loudness?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amplitude**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Amplitude** is the height of a sound wave and directly determines the **loudness** of the sound.
 
• The greater the amplitude of a sound wave, the **louder** the sound it produces.
 
• Amplitude is measured in **decibels (dB)**, which is a logarithmic unit representing sound intensity.
 
• For example, a whisper has a low amplitude, while a shout has a high amplitude, resulting in greater loudness.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wavelength**

 
 
• The distance between two successive crests or troughs of a sound wave.
 
• It determines the type of sound but does not directly affect its loudness.
 
 
 
• **Pitch**
 
 
• Pitch is determined by the **frequency** of the sound wave.
 
• Higher frequency results in a higher pitch, while lower frequency results in a lower pitch.
 
 
 
• **Frequency**
 
 
• Frequency is the number of sound wave cycles per second, measured in **Hertz (Hz)**.
 
• While frequency affects pitch, it does not influence the loudness of the sound.
 
 
 
• **Decibel Scale**
 
 
• Loudness is measured in decibels (dB), with 0 dB being the threshold of human hearing.
 
• Sounds above 85 dB for prolonged periods can cause hearing damage.

questions.question: What is the role of the ribosome in a cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Protein synthesis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary role of the **ribosome** in a cell is **protein synthesis**. Ribosomes act as the cellular machinery that translates genetic code into functional proteins, which are essential for all life processes. ***Hence, the correct option is Protein synthesis.***
 
• Ribosomes are composed of two major components: **ribosomal RNA (rRNA)** and **proteins**. They consist of a **large subunit** and a **small subunit** that come together during the process of translation.
 
• In a cell, ribosomes can be found in two locations: either floating freely in the **cytoplasm** or attached to the surface of the **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER)**. Proteins synthesized on the **RER** are typically destined for secretion or membrane insertion, while free ribosomes synthesize proteins for use within the **cytoplasm**.
 
• The process conducted by ribosomes is known as **Translation**. During this phase, the ribosome reads the sequence of the **messenger RNA (mRNA)** and, with the help of **transfer RNA (tRNA)**, assembles **amino acids** in the correct order to form a **polypeptide chain**.
 
• Ribosomes are universal organelles, meaning they are found in both **prokaryotic** (e.g., bacteria) and **eukaryotic** (e.g., plants and animals) cells, highlighting their fundamental importance in biology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Discovery and Characteristics:**
 
 
• Ribosomes were first observed in the mid-**1950s** by the Romanian-American cell biologist **George Palade** using an electron microscope. He was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine** in **1974** for this discovery.
 
• In **prokaryotes**, the ribosomes are smaller, known as **70S** ribosomes (consisting of **30S** and **50S** subunits). In **eukaryotes**, they are larger, known as **80S** ribosomes (consisting of **40S** and **60S** subunits). The **"S"** stands for the **Svedberg unit**, a measure of sedimentation rate.
 
 
 
• **Energy Production (Option A):**
 
 
• **Energy production** is the primary function of the **Mitochondria**, often called the "Powerhouse of the cell." This organelle generates **Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP)** through the process of **cellular respiration**. ***Hence, statement A is incorrect regarding ribosomes.***
 
 
 
• **Cell Division (Option C):**
 
 
• The process of **cell division** is facilitated by organelles like **centrioles** and **centrosomes** in animal cells, which help in the formation of **spindle fibers**. The **nucleus** plays the leading role by managing **DNA replication**. ***Hence, statement C is incorrect regarding ribosomes.***
 
 
 
• **Transport of Substances (Option D):**
 
 
• The **transport of substances** within and out of the cell is handled by the **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)** and the **Golgi Apparatus** (or Golgi Complex). The Golgi apparatus acts as a "post office," packaging and labeling proteins for their specific **locations**. ***Hence, statement D is incorrect regarding ribosomes.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ribozymes:** While most enzymes are proteins, some **RNA** molecules in the ribosome possess catalytic activity. These are called **ribozymes**, and they are responsible for forming the **peptide bonds** between amino acids.
 
• **Antibiotic Target:** Because **bacterial (70S)** ribosomes differ in structure from **human (80S)** ribosomes, many **antibiotics** (such as **Tetracycline** and **Erythromycin**) work by specifically targeting and inhibiting bacterial ribosomes without harming the host's cells.
 
• **Polysomes:** Often, multiple ribosomes attach to a single **mRNA** strand simultaneously to produce multiple copies of a protein quickly; this complex is known as a **polyribosome** or **polysome**.
</ul

questions.question: The motion of the moon around the earth is due to the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**centripetal force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The motion of the **Moon** around the **Earth** is a form of **circular motion** (specifically, an elliptical orbit that is nearly circular). For any object to maintain a circular path, it requires a force acting towards the center of the circle.
 
• This "center-seeking" force is known as **centripetal force**. It is not a new kind of force but a role played by an existing force in the system. ***Hence, the correct answer is centripetal force.***
 
• In the **Earth-Moon system**, the necessary **centripetal force** is provided by the **gravitational force** of attraction between the **Earth** and the **Moon**.
 
• If this **centripetal force** were absent, the **Moon** would cease its orbital motion and fly off in a straight line along the **tangent** to the circular path due to **inertia**.
 
• The **centripetal force** causes a continuous change in the **direction** of the **Moon's velocity** at every point in its orbit, which means the **Moon** is constantly **accelerating** towards the **Earth**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton’s Law of Universal Gravitation**: Formulated in **1687** by **Sir Isaac Newton**, it states that every particle attracts every other particle in the universe with a force that is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers.
 
• **Magnetic Field**: This refers to the region around a magnetic material or a moving electric charge within which the force of magnetism acts. While the **Earth** has a strong **magnetic field** (the **magnetosphere**), it does not govern the orbital motion of celestial bodies like the **Moon**.
 
• **Friction Force**: This is a force that resists the relative motion of solid surfaces, fluid layers, and material elements sliding against each other. Since space is a **vacuum**, there is no air or surface to provide **friction** to the **Moon**; if friction were present, the **Moon** would eventually lose energy and crash into the **Earth**.
 
• **Acceleration**: While the **Moon** does experience **centripetal acceleration**, acceleration is the **effect** of the force, not the **cause** of the motion. The question asks for the force "due to" which the motion occurs.
 
• **Uniform Circular Motion**: When an object moves in a circle at a **constant speed**, its **velocity** is constantly changing because its direction is changing. This change in velocity over time is what defines **acceleration** in an orbit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Orbital Speed**: The **Moon** travels at an average speed of approximately **1.022 kilometers per second** (about **3,679 km/h**) to maintain its balance between **gravity** and **inertia**.
 
• **Distance**: The average distance from the **Earth** to the **Moon** is approximately **384,400 kilometers**. This distance is critical in calculating the magnitude of the **gravitational force**.
 
• **Revolution Period**: It takes the **Moon** about **27.3 days** to complete one **sidereal revolution** around the **Earth**.
 
• **Satellite Motion**: The same principles of **centripetal force** and **gravity** apply to **artificial satellites** launched by organizations like **ISRO** or **NASA**. To stay in orbit, they must reach a specific **orbital velocity**.
 
• **Tidal Effects**: The **gravitational pull** of the **Moon** on the **Earth's** oceans is the primary cause of **tides**, demonstrating that the force is mutual as per **Newton's Third Law of Motion**.

questions.question: What happens to the pupil in low light conditions?

options.text: It contracts to prevent excess light from entering
It expands to allow more light to enter

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It expands to allow more light to enter**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **pupil** is the dark circular opening in the center of the **iris** that regulates the amount of light entering the eye.
 
• In **low light conditions** or darkness, the pupil **dilates** (expands). This is a physiological response to allow the maximum possible amount of light to reach the **retina**, helping the person see better in the dark.
 
• This expansion is controlled by the **radial muscles** of the iris, which contract to pull the pupil open wider.
 
• In contrast, in **bright light**, the pupil **constricts** (shrinks) to prevent too much light from entering, which could damage the sensitive cells of the retina. This is controlled by the **circular muscles** of the iris.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **iris** is the colored part of the eye that acts like a shutter in a camera, adjusting the size of the pupil.
 
• The adjustment of the pupil size in response to light intensity is known as the **pupillary light reflex**.
 
• The **retina** contains two main types of photoreceptor cells: **rods**, which are sensitive to low light levels (scotopic vision), and **cones**, which are responsible for color vision and high spatial acuity (photopic vision).
 
• The **optic nerve** transmits the visual information from the retina to the **brain** for processing.

questions.question: What is the first law of motion also known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Law of inertia**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion** states that an object will continue to be in a state of rest or in a state of uniform motion along a straight line unless acted upon by an **external unbalanced force**.
 
• This law is also known as the **Law of Inertia** because it describes the inherent property of an object to resist any change in its state of motion.
 
• **Inertia** is the tendency of objects to keep doing what they are doing. If an object is at rest, it wants to stay at rest; if it is moving, it wants to keep moving at the same speed and in the same direction.
 
• **Law of acceleration** refers to **Newton's Second Law**, which states that the force acting on an object is equal to the mass of that object times its acceleration (F = ma).
 
• **Law of action and reaction** refers to **Newton's Third Law**, which states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
• **Law of momentum** is closely related to the Second Law, as force is defined as the rate of change of **linear momentum**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of inertia was first formulated by **Galileo Galilei** for horizontal motion on Earth and was later generalized by **Sir Isaac Newton**.
 
• **Mass** is a quantitative measure of inertia. The more mass an object has, the greater its inertia and the harder it is to change its state of motion.
 
• Newton's laws were first published in his seminal work titled **Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica** in **1687**.
 
• There are three types of inertia: **Inertia of rest**, **Inertia of motion**, and **Inertia of direction**.

questions.question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the **correct **options:

**Assertion (A):** Delhi frequently records the highest AQI levels among Indian cities.

**Reason (R):** It lies in a low-lying basin surrounded by the Himalayas.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A is true but R is false.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assertion (A):** Delhi frequently records the highest **Air Quality Index (AQI)** levels among Indian cities, especially during winter. **✔ True**
 
• **Reason (R):** Delhi does **not** lie in a low-lying basin surrounded by the Himalayas. **✘ False**
 
• Delhi is located on the **Indo-Gangetic Plain**. Although the Himalayas influence regional weather patterns and can reduce the dispersion of pollutants during winter, Delhi is **not situated in a basin enclosed by the Himalayas**.
 
• The major causes of Delhi's high AQI include:
 
 
• Vehicular emissions
 
• Industrial pollution
 
• Construction dust
 
• Crop residue (stubble) burning in neighbouring states
 
• Unfavourable winter meteorological conditions such as low wind speed and temperature inversion
 
 
 
• ***Hence, Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Air Quality Index (AQI):**

 
 
• A measure used to indicate the level of air pollution.
 
• In India, AQI is monitored by the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)**.
 
 
 
• **Factors affecting AQI in Delhi:**
 
 
• High emission sources.
 
• Low wind speed during winter.
 
• Temperature inversion that traps pollutants near the ground.
 
• Seasonal stubble burning in neighbouring states.
 
 

39

questions.question: Some plants like the pea plant climb up other plants or fences by means of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tendrils**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tendrils** are specialized, thread-like structures that are sensitive to touch. They are modified **stems, leaves, or even petioles** used by climbing plants for support.
 
• In the case of the **pea plant** (**Pisum sativum**), the **terminal leaflets** of the compound leaf are modified into **tendrils**. These structures help the plant, which has a **weak stem**, to climb up supports like **fences, sticks, or other plants**.
 
• When a **tendril** comes into contact with any support, the side of the tendril in contact with the object does not grow as rapidly as the side away from the object. This **differential growth** causes the tendril to **coil** around the support.
 
• The growth movement of a plant part in response to **touch** is known as **thigmotropism**. This is the physiological principle that allows climbing plants to anchor themselves effectively.
 
• The primary function of these structures is to allow **weak-stemmed plants** to ascend toward **sunlight**, which is essential for the process of **photosynthesis**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Thorns**: These are hard, pointed, and sharp structures which are modifications of the **axillary buds** of the **stem**. They are commonly found in plants like **Citrus** and **Bougainvillea**. Their main function is **protection** from browsing animals and to reduce **transpiration** in some desert plants.
 
• **Root hair**: These are tiny, unicellular outgrowths of the **root epidermis** (epiblema) found in the **region of maturation**. They play a critical role in increasing the surface area for the **absorption of water and minerals** from the soil through the process of **osmosis**.
 
• **Cell sap**: This is the fluid located inside the **vacuole** of a plant cell. It is a dilute solution of **minerals, salts, sugars, and amino acids**. It serves to maintain **turgor pressure** within the cell, providing mechanical strength and support to non-woody plant parts, but it is not an organ for climbing.
 
• **Modified Stems vs. Modified Leaves**: It is important to note that while tendrils in **peas** are modified **leaves**, in other plants like **grapes (Vitis vinifera)**, the tendrils are modified **stems**. Both serve the same climbing function, illustrating **homoplasy** or convergent evolution.
 
• **Other Climbing Mechanisms**: Some plants use **climbing roots** (e.g., **Money plant** or **Piper betle**) which arise from the nodes and internodes to attach the plant to a vertical surface. Others, known as **twiners**, simply wrap their entire main stem around a support.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding electromagnetic devices?

options.text: Electric Generator : Converts electrical energy to mechanical energy.
Transformer : Operates on DC current to change voltage.
Electric Bell : Uses the magnetic effect of electric current.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electric Bell: Uses the magnetic effect of electric current.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An electric bell operates on the principle of the **magnetic effect of electric current**, where an electromagnet is created by passing an electric current through a coil of wire.
 
• The magnetic field generated attracts a metal armature, causing it to strike the bell and produce sound.
 
• The electric bell consists of components like an electromagnet, armature, contact screw, and hammer, all working in synchronization to create the ringing sound.
 
• When the circuit is complete, the current flows through the coil, magnetizing the core, and pulling the armature, which simultaneously breaks the circuit and causes the hammer to strike the bell.
 
• This cycle repeats rapidly as long as the switch is pressed, producing a continuous ringing sound.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electric Generator: Converts electrical energy to mechanical energy**

 
 
• This statement is incorrect. An electric generator actually converts **mechanical energy into electrical energy**.
 
• It operates on the principle of electromagnetic induction, as discovered by Michael Faraday, where a conductor moving through a magnetic field induces an electric current.
 
• Generators are widely used in power plants to produce electricity for homes, industries, and businesses.
 
 
 
• **Transformer: Operates on DC current to change voltage**
 
 
• This statement is incorrect because transformers **only work with alternating current (AC)**, not direct current (DC).
 
• Transformers are used to step up (increase) or step down (decrease) the voltage levels in an AC circuit.
 
• They function based on the principle of mutual induction between two coils of wire.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnet: A permanent magnet**
 
 
• This statement is incorrect because an electromagnet is a **temporary magnet** that only exhibits magnetic properties when an electric current flows through its coil.
 
• Once the current is stopped, the magnetic field disappears, unlike a permanent magnet that retains its magnetism.
 
• Electromagnets are widely used in devices like motors, relays, and magnetic cranes.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the relationship between velocity and acceleration in different dimensions?

options.text: In one-dimensional motion, velocity and acceleration are always perpendicular to each other.
In two-dimensional motion, acceleration must always act opposite to velocity.
In one-dimensional motion, velocity and acceleration lie along the same line, either in the same or opposite direction.
In three-dimensional motion, velocity and acceleration must always act in the same direction.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**In one-dimensional motion, velocity and acceleration lie along the same line, either in the same or opposite direction.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **One-dimensional motion**, also known as **rectilinear motion**, refers to movement along a straight line. In this case, the position of the object can be described using a single coordinate (e.g., x).
 
• The **velocity** vector always points in the direction of motion along that straight line.
 
• **Acceleration** is defined as the rate of change of velocity. For the motion to remain strictly one-dimensional, any change in the velocity must occur along the same axis. Therefore, acceleration must act along the same line as velocity.
 
• If **velocity and acceleration** are in the **same direction**, the object is **speeding up**.
 
• If **velocity and acceleration** are in **opposite directions**, the object is **slowing down** (also known as **deceleration** or **retardation**).
 
• In **two-dimensional** or **three-dimensional** motion, acceleration can be at any angle to the velocity vector, which allows the object to change its **direction** of motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In **Uniform Circular Motion**, the acceleration (centripetal acceleration) is always **perpendicular** to the velocity vector. This changes the direction of the object but not its speed.
 
• In **Projectile Motion** (a type of 2D motion), the acceleration due to gravity is constant and acts vertically downwards, while the velocity has both horizontal and vertical components.
 
• **Instantaneous velocity** is the derivative of position with respect to time, and **instantaneous acceleration** is the derivative of velocity with respect to time.
 
• If acceleration is **zero**, the velocity remains **constant** in both magnitude and direction.

questions.question: Among the following organs, which is located on uppermost part of a human body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Buccal Cavity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **buccal cavity**, also known as the oral cavity or mouth, is located in the **uppermost part of the human body** compared to other options like the anus, bile duct, or appendix.
 
• It is the entry point for the digestive system and is responsible for several critical functions, such as the ingestion of food, mechanical digestion through chewing, and mixing food with saliva for initial digestion.
 
• The buccal cavity is situated in the head region and contains structures like the **teeth, tongue, and salivary glands**, which are essential for the process of digestion and speech.
 
• Being in the head, the buccal cavity is anatomically positioned above the other body parts mentioned in the options.
 
• Its strategic placement at the uppermost part of the body ensures the smooth intake of food and air, a vital function for the survival of humans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Anatomical Position of the Buccal Cavity:**

 
 
• The buccal cavity is located in the facial region of the skull.
 
• It is bordered by the lips in the front, cheeks on the sides, the palate on top, and the floor of the mouth below.
 
• It opens posteriorly into the pharynx, which connects to both the digestive and respiratory systems.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Buccal Cavity:**
 
 
• **Ingestion:** It is the entry point for food and fluids into the digestive system.
 
• **Chewing:** The teeth grind food into smaller particles, while the tongue helps in mixing food with saliva.
 
• **Speech:** The tongue, lips, and teeth work together to produce sounds and facilitate communication.
 
• **Taste Perception:** Taste buds on the tongue detect different flavors.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Options:**
 
 
• **Anus:** Located at the lowermost part of the body, it serves as the exit point of the digestive system.
 
• **Bile Duct:** Found in the abdominal region, it transports bile from the liver and gallbladder to the small intestine.
 
• **Appendix:** A vestigial organ attached to the cecum (part of the large intestine), located in the lower right abdomen.
 
 
 
• **Interesting Facts:**
 
 
• The buccal cavity contains approximately 700 species of bacteria, forming an essential part of the oral microbiome.
 
• Saliva, secreted by the salivary glands in the buccal cavity, contains enzymes like amylase that begin the breakdown of carbohydrates.
 
• Humans have 32 teeth in adulthood, which are categorized into incisors, canines, premolars, and molars, all located within the buccal cavity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of the Buccal Cavity in Digestion:**

 
 
• The buccal cavity is the site for the first phase of digestion, where food is broken down mechanically by teeth and chemically by saliva.
 
• Saliva contains enzymes like **salivary amylase**, which begins the digestion of starch into maltose.
 
 
 
• **Oral Hygiene and Health:**
 
 
• Maintaining oral hygiene is crucial as infections in the buccal cavity can lead to systemic diseases.
 
• Common diseases include dental caries, gingivitis, and oral thrush.

questions.question: Which of the following celestial bodies is classified as a dwarf planet?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pluto**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pluto** was officially reclassified from a major planet to a **dwarf planet** by the **International Astronomical Union (IAU)** in **August 2006**.
 
• The IAU defines a planet based on three criteria: it must **orbit the Sun**, it must have **sufficient mass** to assume a nearly round shape (hydrostatic equilibrium), and it must have **cleared the neighborhood** around its orbit.
 
• While Pluto orbits the Sun and is spherical, it has not cleared its orbital path of other debris, as it resides in the **Kuiper Belt** alongside many other icy objects.
 
• **Jupiter**, **Earth**, and **Venus** are all classified as **major planets** because they satisfy all three criteria, including clearing their respective orbital neighborhoods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are currently five recognized dwarf planets in our solar system: **Pluto**, **Eris**, **Haumea**, **Makemake**, and **Ceres**.
 
• **Ceres** is the smallest of the dwarf planets and the only one located in the **asteroid belt** between **Mars** and **Jupiter**.
 
• **Eris**, discovered in **2005**, is more massive than Pluto, which triggered the debate leading to the new definition of a planet.
 
• Dwarf planets are distinct from **natural satellites** (moons) because they orbit the Sun directly rather than orbiting another planet.

questions.question: What is the result of the uneven growth of the tendril in response to touch?

options.text: The tendril circles around the object and clings to it
The tendril falls off the plant

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The tendril circles around the object and clings to it**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Tendrils** are specialized plant structures that help plants climb and support themselves by attaching to nearby objects, such as a trellis or neighboring plants. 
• When a tendril comes in contact with an object, cells on the side touching the object grow slower, while cells on the opposite side elongate faster. This uneven growth causes the tendril to **curl around the object**. 
• This process is a type of growth movement in response to touch, known as **thigmotropism**. It enables plants to maximize sunlight exposure by climbing toward light sources. 
• The coiling around the object strengthens the plant's anchorage and prevents the tendril from falling off, ensuring stability. 
• Examples of plants with tendrils include **pea plants (Pisum sativum)**, **grapevines (Vitis vinifera)**, and **cucumber plants (Cucumis sativus)**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Thigmotropism:** 
• It is a plant's directional growth response to touch or physical contact with a solid object. 
• In tendrils, this response is facilitated by differential growth rates in cells on opposite sides of the tendril. 
• Other examples of thigmotropism include the coiling of climbing plants such as ivy and the folding of leaves in **Mimosa pudica** when touched. 
• **Types of Tropisms:** 
• **Phototropism:** Growth movement in response to light (e.g., sunflower turning toward sunlight). 
• **Geotropism:** Growth movement in response to gravity (e.g., roots growing downward). 
• **Hydrotropism:** Growth movement in response to water (e.g., roots growing toward water sources). 
• **Thigmotropism:** Growth in response to touch (e.g., tendrils coiling around objects). 
• **Functions of Tendrils:** 
• Provide structural support to weak-stemmed plants. 
• Help plants climb and reach sunlight for photosynthesis. 
• Reduce the risk of being overshadowed by competing vegetation. 
• **Examples of Tendril-Bearing Plants:** 
• **Pea plant (Pisum sativum):** Has leaf tendrils to support climbing. 
• **Grapevine (Vitis vinifera):** Uses tendrils for attachment and climbing. 
• **Passionflower (Passiflora):** Features tendrils for structural support. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Key Characteristics of Tendrils:** 
• Tendrils may originate from leaves, leaflets, or stems depending on the plant species. 
• They are highly sensitive to touch, allowing them to detect and respond to nearby objects. 
• Once coiled, tendrils develop lignin to strengthen their structure and hold the plant securely. 
• **Scientific Explanation:** 
• The coiling is driven by differential auxin distribution. **Auxin**, a plant hormone, accumulates on the side away from the contact point, promoting cell elongation and causing curvature. 
• Other hormones like **ethylene** may also play a role in regulating thigmotropic responses. </ul

questions.question: How many chambers are there in the heart of amphibians?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Amphibians possess a **three-chambered heart**, which is a significant evolutionary step from the two-chambered hearts seen in fish.
 
• The heart structure consists of **two atria** (the right atrium and the left atrium) and **one single ventricle**.
 
• The **right atrium** receives **deoxygenated blood** from the various body organs, while the **left atrium** receives **oxygenated blood** from the **lungs** and the **skin** (which also acts as a respiratory organ).
 
• Both atria pump blood into the single **ventricle**, where some degree of **mixing** of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood occurs before it is pumped out to the rest of the body and the respiratory surfaces.
 
• This arrangement facilitates **double circulation**, although it is considered **incomplete** because the oxygenated and deoxygenated blood streams are not fully separated in the ventricle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fish (Pisces)**:

 
 
• Fish have a **two-chambered heart** consisting of **one atrium** and **one ventricle**.
 
• They exhibit **single circulation**, where the heart pumps deoxygenated blood to the **gills**, and from there, it goes directly to the rest of the body.
 
 
 
• **Reptiles**:
 
 
• Most reptiles have a **three-chambered heart** with a **partially divided ventricle**, which reduces the mixing of blood.
 
• However, **crocodiles**, **alligators**, and **gavials** are unique among reptiles as they possess a fully functional **four-chambered heart**.
 
 
 
• **Birds and Mammals**:
 
 
• These groups possess a **four-chambered heart** with **two atria** and **two ventricles**.
 
• This structure ensures the **complete separation** of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, allowing for high **metabolic efficiency** required for **warm-blooded** (endothermic) animals.
 
 
 
• **Amphibian Respiration**:
 
 
• Because the **three-chambered heart** allows for some blood mixing, amphibians (such as **frogs**, **toads**, and **salamanders**) often supplement their oxygen intake through **cutaneous respiration** (breathing through their **moist skin**).
 
• This is particularly important during periods when they are submerged in water or during **hibernation**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **atrium** is the receiving chamber of the heart, while the **ventricle** is the main pumping chamber.
 
• In **Amphibians**, the **3** chambers allow for a more complex circulatory route called the **pulmocutaneous circuit**, which directs blood to the gas-exchange tissues in the lungs and skin.
 
• The evolution of the heart from **2** chambers in fish to **3** in amphibians and finally **4** in mammals reflects the increasing energy demands of animals as they moved from aquatic to terrestrial environments.

questions.question: Why should we wear cotton clothes in summer?

options.text: Cotton clothes prevent any evaporation of sweat.
Cotton clothes increase the body temperature by trapping heat.
Cotton clothes absorb sweat and help in its evaporation, which cools the body.
Cotton clothes are less absorbent and keep sweat on the skin.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cotton clothes absorb sweat and help in its evaporation, which cools the body**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cotton** is a **natural fiber** that is highly **hydrophilic**, meaning it has a high capacity to **absorb water** or **moisture**.
 
• During **summer**, the human body produces more **sweat** as a biological mechanism to maintain **homeostasis** and regulate **internal temperature**.
 
• When we wear **cotton clothes**, the fabric **absorbs the sweat** from our skin and brings it into contact with the **atmosphere**.
 
• The **evaporation** of this sweat requires **energy**, which is taken from the **body surface** in the form of **heat**. This process is known as **evaporative cooling**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Cotton clothes prevent any evaporation of sweat**: This is incorrect because cotton actually facilitates evaporation by wicking moisture to the surface. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Cotton clothes increase the body temperature by trapping heat**: Synthetic fibers like **wool** or certain **polyesters** trap heat, but cotton is **breathable** and allows heat to escape. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Cotton clothes are less absorbent**: In reality, cotton can absorb up to **25 times** its weight in water, making it more absorbent than most **synthetic fabrics**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Latent Heat of Vaporization**: This is the **thermal energy** required to convert a liquid into a **gas** without changing its temperature. In the context of **summer cooling**, the sweat on the skin absorbs this **latent heat** from the body to evaporate, thereby **lowering the body temperature**.
 
• **Porosity of Cotton**: Cotton fibers are naturally **porous**. This **porosity** allows for better **air circulation** (breathability), which aids the **evaporation process** and prevents the growth of **bacteria** or **fungi** that thrive in stagnant, moist environments.
 
• **Comparison with Synthetic Fabrics**: Fabrics like **nylon** or **polyester** are **hydrophobic**. They do not absorb **sweat** effectively, causing it to remain trapped between the skin and the cloth, leading to **discomfort**, **skin rashes**, and a feeling of **suffocation** in **humid weather**.
 
• **Hypoallergenic Properties**: Cotton is a **hypoallergenic** material, making it ideal for **sensitive skin** during **summer** when **sweat-induced irritation** and **heat rashes** are common.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Color Matters**: In addition to the material, the **color** of the clothing is vital in **summer**. **Light-colored** cotton clothes reflect most of the **solar radiation** (heat) falling on them, whereas **dark colors** absorb it.
 
• **Molecular Structure**: The **cellulose** molecules in cotton contain **hydroxyl (-OH) groups** that attract **water molecules**, explaining its high **absorbency** compared to **petroleum-based** synthetic fibers.
 
• **Homeostasis**: The body's ability to keep its **internal environment** stable. **Sweating** is a primary method of **thermoregulation**, and choosing the right fabric like **cotton** assists the body in this **physiological** task.
